chunks: And they denied, and followed their own vain desires; but every matter is determined at its time.

key_terms.أَهْوَاءَهُمْ: their own vain desires or whims
key_terms.مُسْتَقِرٌّ: determined, settled, or fixed at its time

ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about those who follow their own desires instead of divine guidance?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the psychological state of the Meccan disbelievers who, despite clear signs, chose to follow their *ahwa'* (base desires) over divine truth, a theme central to the concept of *Tawhid* in action. The phrase 'every matter is settled' (*kullu amrin mustaqirr*) is interpreted by scholars like Allamah Tabatabai as referring to the fixed decree of Allah, ensuring that both the punishment of the disbelievers and the ultimate victory of the Prophet (SAW) are inevitable and precisely timed. This reinforces the Shia belief in divine justice (*Adl*), where no deed goes unnoticed and every soul will face the consequences of its choices on the Day of Judgment.
